Security update for Vito PostgreSQL Manager. Upgrade from 0.1.0 before production use.

## Security fixes

- Database names are quoted as literal values inside fixed libpq connection parameters. Names containing `=`, URI prefixes, quotes or backslashes can no longer override the selected endpoint in SQL, backup or restore operations.
- Administrative connections restrict `search_path` to `pg_catalog` at startup and before SQL, preventing application-owned functions from intercepting privileged queries.
- Generated release metadata now follows the plugin version.

## Validation

- **26 Linux unit tests passed.**
- **Six live PostgreSQL 18.6 security regressions passed** in a fresh offline sandbox with read-only source/toolchain, dummy principals, private scratch storage and resource limits.
- Both 0.1.0 issues were reproduced with harmless negative controls. The patched worker passed literal-name SQL, custom backup and data-verified restore, existing-target refusal, administrative schema queries and application grants under a hostile search path.
- Vito host installation/lifecycle and authorization checks run in GitHub Actions.

See [security fixes and exact test scope](https://github.com/techibytesmedia/vito-postgresql-manager/blob/v0.1.1/docs/SECURITY.md).

## Install or update

In **Admin → Plugins → Install**, use:

`https://github.com/techibytesmedia/vito-postgresql-manager`

For an existing installation, disable the plugin, wait for active operations,
update to **v0.1.1**, then re-enable. The namespace and metadata schema are unchanged.
Database contents, ownership and existing grants are preserved by this update.

This build targets **Vito 4.1.1 / PHP 8.4+** and Ubuntu 24.04 with PostgreSQL 18.
Live worker regressions were run on **x86_64**. **ARM64 functional verification,
S3 transfers and a Linux Vito control-application runtime remain unverified.**
This focused security remediation is not a full independent audit.
